brief_extract: Miss Dillon regrets that her only recollection of that early meeting is "of a dark, heavily furnished room with a lot of strangers seated round a large, shining dining table". Her diary contains frequent entries of 'electrical meetings' held early in 1925 at 25 George Street. A young woman academically in the forefront of her generation, Miss Dillon was invited to become a Founder Member of the EAW and with her special knowledge she was able to give considerable assistance to the Association in its early years.

location_standardised: London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Institution where Tess Dillon worked during her career.
brief_extract: Miss Dillon's own very busy career precluded her being as involved with the Association as she would have wished. Convinced of the importance of extending knowledge of domestic electricity, Miss Dillon organised a series of holiday training courses at QEC in the early 1930's for demonstrators and teachers.

article_title: A PLACE IN THE SUN The House of the Future?
brief_extract:
A PLACE IN THE SUN

The House of
the Future? Future 1 Photovoltaic Home

A situation whereby a householder can produce all the electricity necessary for his own domestic needs plus a surplus which he can sell to the electricity utility may have a touch of Alice in Wonderland about it but if an experiment now being conducted by the Georgia Power Company in Atlanta, USA is proved to be successful it could become a feasible proposition in the near future. Called Future 1, a house described as the nation's first extensively monitored photo-voltaic home is a four bedroomed dwelling looking like many other upper middle class American houses, except for a 16ft x 32ft array of photovoltaic cell collectors (which allow direct conversion of the sun's rays into electricity) on its south facing roof.
